_comment: Argument-value domains TradingView enforces at RUNTIME (RE-class errors) and documents nowhere in the reference prose. Backs TODO #69. Each fact is transcribed from a chart-legend banner held in scripts/probes/re-class-runtime-errors/tv-banners/ - the images are the primary source, this file is the machine-readable transcription. NOT re-derivable from either pine-lint mode: RE-class errors reach neither (see gotchas/G010), so a fact may only be added here with a banner behind it. Consumed by packages/pipeline/src/generate.ts, which merges min/max/notNa into the affected parameter in pine-data/v6/functions.json.

facts.quote: Invalid value of the 'length' argument (0) in the "sma" function. It must be > 0.
Invalid value of the 'length' argument in the "sma" function. It must not be na
Invalid value of the 'leftbars' argument (-1) in the 'pivothigh' function. It must be >= 0.

_notAdded._comment: Domains observed but deliberately NOT baked in, each with the reason. Removing an entry from here means new evidence arrived, not that someone changed their mind.
_notAdded.ta.sma.length.max: RE10004 caps historical references at 5000, but that is ONE banner from ONE script and it is unestablished whether the ceiling is per-call, global, or interacts with max_bars_back. A max: 5000 here would flag every long-lookback call on an assumption. See TODO #69's open question.
_notAdded.ta.pivotlow.leftbars: Symmetric with ta.pivothigh by every reasonable expectation - and expectation is exactly what this file does not record. Needs its own banner.
_notAdded.ta.ema/ta.rma/... .length: The '> 0' domain almost certainly holds for every ta.* length parameter, but 'almost certainly' is what manufactured the retracted G002. One chart capture per function is the price of each row.
_notAdded.array.slice.index_from/index_to: RE10044 (inverted constant range) is a relation BETWEEN two arguments, which the per-parameter min/max shape here cannot express. Banner captured (RE10044-slice-inverted-range.png); needs a cross-parameter fact shape first.
